overview.description: Droggn is a rare Tyrolean trick-taking game from the Stubai Valley, historically played with a unique 66-card Tarock deck. It is a descendant of the Tarock L'Hombre family, making it distinct from more common Austrian variants like KÃ¶nigrufen. Known for its specific Tyrolean dialect terminology and the tactical use of the 'Fox' card, the game survived in the alpine villages of Fulpmes and Telfes as a testament to localized card-playing traditions.

history.origins: The game is centered in the Stubaital (Stubai Valley) southwest of Innsbruck. Its introduction is shrouded in legend, with roots potentially tied to Tyrolean resistance hero Andreas Hofer or traveling Italian merchants.
timeline: 1800s: Traditional Tarock patterns begin to specialize in alpine valleys.
Early 20th Century: Specific 66-card packs for Droggn were commercially available.
1990s: Rules formalized and archived to prevent extinction of the Stubai tradition.
history.evolution: Preserves game mechanics from the early 19th century L'Hombre games that disappeared elsewhere in the Habsburg Empire.
history.cultural: Integral to Tyrolean tavern culture; the term 'Droggn' effectively means 'the local way of playing Tarock'.

setup.deck: 66-card deck (Industrie und Glück pattern with lowest cards removed). 22 Tarocks, 44 suit cards.
setup.dealing: 21 cards per player, dealt in batches of 7. 3-card talon face down in centre.

rules.objective: As declarer, take at least 37 card points (half of 74) in tricks to win the contract.
rules.gameplay:
1. Bidding: Players compete for the contract.
2. Talon Exchange: Declarer can swap cards with the blind.
3. Trick Play: High and low Pip rankings exist. Tarocks always win. Follow suit required; Trumping required if void.
keyRules: The Gstieß (fool) is not a trump; it may be played anytime and never wins except last trick of Super Mord.
Ultimo: A bonus for winning the final trick with the weakest trump (card I, der Kleine).
Point total in pack: 74 card points (counted in threes, minus 2 per group).

strategy.basic: Keep track of the 22 trumps. If you are the declarer, try to clear the defenders' trumps as early as possible.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Fox' play: Intentionally keeping a low card (singleton) to bait defenders into revealing their high court cards.
strategy.advanced: Declarer should keep a long suit to pull trumps, while defenders should try to 'sandwich' the declarer so they play first into a new suit.
tips: Defenders should smear points when their partner wins a trick.

list.name: Deal and talon position
list.description: Talon may be dealt in the middle (e.g. after second batch of 7) rather than at end. One variant: deal in batches of 5-5-5-3-3 then talon.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Deal and talon placement do not change engine constants; variant is descriptive only.

list.name: Exposing the talon
list.description: In ordinary game some players have declarer expose the talon before picking it up; in Solo declarer picks up without showing. Others say declarer never shows the talon.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Talon visibility is a procedural variant not modelled as engine overrides.

list.name: Game with 78 cards
list.description: Played with full 78-card pack. Deal in 5s; declarer needs 39 card points to win. Super Mord score probably 169. Otherwise rules same.
list.emptyOverridesReason: 78-card variant would require different deck and deal constants; not yet modelled.

difficulty.easy: Fails to manage the 3-card talon effectively; poor trump counting.
difficulty.hard: Perfect point-tracking and probability calculations for the L'Hombre-style bidding.

considerations: AI must handle the specific 66-card deck composition and reverse red-suit pip rankings.

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Starting with player to dealer's left, each bids once (Ansager, Solo, Super, Super Mord) or says weiter. Highest bidder becomes declarer.

phases.label: Trick play
phases.notes: Declarer leads first. 21 tricks. Follow suit; if void, trump. Gstieß may be played anytime and does not win (except last trick of Super Mord).

edgeCases.text: Gstieß never wins a trick except last trick of Super Mord.
If Pagat is laid out, holder must keep it until last trick if possible.
Revoke penalty: offending side loses basic game value plus Pagat if laid out, doubled for Schwacher or Retour.

customActions.description: Pass on bidding; do not bid (say 'weiter').
customActions.constraints: Only when it is your turn to bid.

engine.deckDescription: A 66-card French-suited tarock deck with 21 trumps plus the Fool and 44 suit cards. Black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10 down to 4; red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace down to 7.
engine.suitDescription: Spades and Clubs are the long black suits; Hearts and Diamonds are the round red suits. The two colour groups keep different pip subsets.
engine.rankDescription: Courts are King, Queen, Cavalier, and Jack. The long black suits rank 10 down to 4 beneath the courts; the round red suits rank Ace down to 7 beneath the courts.
engine.dealPattern: 7 cards per batch to each player, three batches; 3-card talon.
